Definition: from G4183 and G5092; extremely valuable:--very costly, of great price.
BiblicalUsage: Polytimos is its close cousin, extremely valuable, of great price. John uses it for Mary's spikenard, and Peter for faith that is more precious than gold tried in the fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that faith is the most valuable thing I own, and unlike gold it only grows more precious under fire.
